analysis:
The only change is docs/reference/configuration.md, head lines 320-323. It adds four env-var documentation rows: DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP, _MTP_DEPTH, _MTP_VERIFICATION and _SUPER_MAX_CONCURRENT. No code, control, endpoint or deployment change is in the supplied evidence.

Security-relevant claims in the new rows:
- All are opt-in, off by default, and not forwarded to LaunchAgents, so they apply only to foreground/local runs.
- DARKBLOOM_CBV2_MTP still acts as a kill switch.
- The speculating owner refuses media.
- Invalid values, or MAX_CONCURRENT above 1 combined with MTP=1, fail the load. The docs describe this as fail-closed behavior.
- These controls do not touch the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), App Attest authorization (TB-011) or attestation (TB-009).

The change touches no assets and weakens no mitigation, and no threat-model entry is invalidated.

Possible indirect tie-in: T-041 concerns the prefix cache. Concurrent batched decode, if combined with the prefix cache, might affect the T-041 timing channel. The supplied evidence does not show this, so it is only a note.

The NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift and NemotronSuperLocalAdmission.swift implementations were not supplied. The documented behavior is unverified. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the head units show the full rows, and no base-side lines changed.

No findings.
